PROGRAMMES / GEAR FOR GOLD

Academy-driven. Coach-led. Athlete-centric.

Gear for Gold strengthens athlete-centric academies across India by supporting them with sports science, infrastructure, technology, and performance systems to drive long-term excellence.

Gear for Gold, an initiative of the Infosys Foundation, is designed to build stronger, athlete-centric academies across India. By using GoSports' Academy Development Model, the programme empowers academies, enables coaches, and drives athlete development for long-term sporting excellence.

Academy-Driven Coach-Led Athlete-Centric
About the partnership

A flagship collaboration

Gear for Gold is a flagship partnership between Infosys Foundation and GoSports Foundation, designed to strengthen athlete-centric academies across India. Building on the Girls for Gold initiative, the programme now supports male, female, and para-athletes across Olympic disciplines.

"Infosys Foundation and GoSports Foundation share a joint passion for strengthening the sports ecosystem in India. We are delighted with the progress we have made together in nurturing exceptional youngsters across sporting disciplines."
Sumit VirmaniGlobal Chief Marketing Officer, Infosys; Trustee, Infosys Foundation
FY 2025–26 snapshot

The programme in numbers

8Academies across 15 states & 2 UTs
70Supported athletes, 6 sports
175Medals won (77 gold, 48 silver, 50 bronze)
564Tournaments (138 international, 426 domestic)

130+ high-performance camps delivered across the year.

The academies

Eight academies at the heart of the programme

Gear for Gold works through eight athlete-centric academies, most of them founded by Olympians and national coaches who now develop the next generation.

SHOOTING · 10M & 50M

Lakshya Shooting Club

Mumbai, Maharashtra · est. 2006

Founded by Olympian and Dronacharya awardee Suma Shirur: a high-performance centre for 10m and 50m shooting.

BOXING

Mary Kom Regional Boxing Foundation

Imphal, Manipur · est. 2005

Set up by Olympic medallist Mary Kom, with residential training for boxers from across the region.

TABLE TENNIS

Raman Table Tennis High Performance Centre

Chetpet, Chennai · est. 2016

Founded by Olympian and Dronacharya awardee S. Raman with former national player Bhuvaneswari B.

BADMINTON

Yadav Pro Badminton Academy

est. 2011

Founded by former international shuttler Jagadish Yadav and recognised under Khelo India.

ACADEMY

Sathish Sivalingam Sports Foundation

Sathuvachari, Vellore · est. 2017

Founded by Olympian and Arjuna awardee Sathish Sivalingam after his 2018 Commonwealth Games gold.

ATHLETICS

Usha School of Athletics

Balussery, Kerala · est. 2000

Founded by Olympian P.T. Usha to train young women athletes in sprints, jumps and middle distance.

BADMINTON

Malik Badminton Academy

Sonepat, Haryana · est. 2012

Founded by Harender Malik, with a structured grassroots-to-international pathway open to underprivileged players.

WEIGHTLIFTING

Karnam Malleswari Foundation

Yamunanagar · est. 2017

Founded by Olympic bronze medallist Karnam Malleswari, with coaching, nutrition and residential support.

Interventions

Pillars of the Academy Development Model

01

Athlete development pathway

A structured system to identify, train, progress, and transition athletes across levels.

02

Coaching & support ecosystem

A tech-driven, integrated support ecosystem around athletes training at the academy.

03

Infrastructure & sports science

International-standard facilities and performance centres built for athlete and coach development.

04

Governance & programme management

Clear governance frameworks that drive decision-making, accountability, and effective delivery.
